# OpenVote

> OpenVote is a Ukrainian open-source project building a free public platform where people can create questions, discuss them, vote and inspect aggregated results. The canonical website is https://openvote.com.ua/.

## Current public status

- The production site currently contains a public demand poll, project information, a 23-question FAQ and a browser-only demo.
- Real identity-verified civic voting is not live yet.
- The public demo at https://openvote.com.ua/demo/ is for interface exploration. Polls, votes, comments and vote IDs created there stay only in that browser and are not real public platform records.
- OpenVote is not a government service, official election, legally binding referendum or automatically representative sociological study.
- A result describes participants in one specific vote. It must not be presented as the opinion of all Ukrainians without a separately designed representative sample and methodology.

## Canonical public pages

- About OpenVote: https://openvote.com.ua/about/

- Result methodology and interpretation: https://openvote.com.ua/methodology/
- Privacy, security and known limits: https://openvote.com.ua/privacy/
- Frequently asked questions: https://openvote.com.ua/faq/
- Browser-only demo: https://openvote.com.ua/demo/

## Verified project boundaries

- The current demand poll is voluntary and self-selected. It does not verify identity, citizenship, age or one-person uniqueness.
- The repository contains a full voting flow implemented and tested with test people and test keys. This is engineering evidence, not an external audit or a live public voting service.
- No external cryptographic, privacy, security or legal report exists yet.
- Absolute anonymity is not guaranteed. The public privacy page documents the intended separation of identity and ballot data plus current known limits.
- The real BankID contract, production identity adapter, final production key-custody model and responsible operator policy remain unfinished.
- There is no committed launch date. The public goal is 10,000 supporting responses together with completion of core functions, identity connection and security checks.
